tasks.behavior: One chain whose RPC hosts are down no longer stops the api, worker and signer: that chain waits until two hosts answer again, and the other chains keep working
acceptance: When an enabled chain's RPC hosts don't answer at startup (fewer than two answer), the api, worker and signer log that chain as unavailable and start, as they already keep running through an outage; nothing is decided paid or settled without the second RPC (D-15), as before. Both roles are asked at once, so a role is checked even when the other is down

A mistake in the chain list or on chain still stops them: a chain missing from the list, a chain listing one host, a role whose hosts all serve another chain, no factory code, or an executor without gas

tasks.behavior: A payer-chooses invoice doesn't close before every option chain was read past its close, so a paid one never shows expired
acceptance: While no option is chosen, the main row of a payer-chooses invoice expires only after every other enabled option chain was read past expires_at, and waits for the R-119 choice when any option has money; so an on-time payment on another option is always recorded and chosen first
The pay and owner pages (ClosedSQL, R-77) follow the same rule, so they don't show expired while that wait lasts
The choice query uses an index (id = $1 OR main_id = $1), not coalesce(main_id, id) = $1, since it runs for more rows

Tests cover both orders: the payment recorded before the main row is processed, and the main chain read past the close before the option chain records an on-time payment; neither paid invoice gets invoice.expired in its history; unit passes
